title: Scan workflow and audit results UI

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 5 — ROUND 1 — VERDICT: CONDITIONAL (three required fixes) Audited commit 04be8992ae99fe9c53e9b3bacdab77dea50dfe38 on main, against base 9b400e7 (Sprint 4 close). Working tree clean; committed code. Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict; unchanged within this commit. No cross-version criterion. One new dependency (undici 8.10.2) — justified, see req 14. The wiring is right. Connection pinning is real, the credential boundary holds exactly where I said it had to, the double-submit guard is server-side, headers and bfcache are inherited from the shared layout, and the tests are thorough on the paths they cover. But three of the sprint's most important requirements — the ones about NOT hiding things from the developer — fail on paths the tests never exercise, and one of them is a script-injection hole. All three are demonstrated below with rendered HTML from the real route, not read off the code. === REQUIRED FIXES === A. [HIGH — injection] A sitemap is rendered into an with no scheme check anywhere between xml.js and the view. views/scan/_item-list.ejs:7; the gap is upstream in lib/sitemap (xml.js readLoc / crawl.js urlset collection accept any string). DEMONSTRATED: staging sitemap containing javascript:alert(document.querySelector('[name=_csrf]').value) → the rendered results page contains . EJS entity-escapes the quotes, which does nothing here — a browser decodes attribute entities before evaluating the javascript: URL. One click on a "page at risk" runs attacker script in the authenticated origin, with the CSRF token in the DOM and every state-changing route (edit credentials, delete project) reachable. The title fetch correctly refuses the URL (UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL) and falls back to a slug — so the item survives into the list. Threat model is real, not theoretical: compromised WordPress installs are routine, and this tool exists to point at client staging sites, some of which will be compromised at some point. Sprint 2's save-time URL validation and Sprint 3's request-time SSRF check both exist because sitemap-adjacent input is untrusted; the URLs INSIDE the sitemap are the same class of input and got no equivalent. FIX (Dev Team's call how): reject non-http(s) values at collection in lib/sitemap (drop the entry and record it in skipped with a reason like 'invalid-url-scheme', so requirement 6's "nothing dropped without a record" still holds) — that protects Sprint 4's title fetcher and any future consumer too, not just this view. A view-layer guard as defence in depth is fine but is not the fix. Test: a fixture urlset with javascript:, data:, and vbscript: locs; assert none reach result.urls and none appear in rendered href attributes. Authoring that test is Dev Team's job. B. [HIGH — requirement 10 not met on its primary path; the sprint's own LiveQA criterion fails] A staging site behind .htaccess with no credentials saved produces the generic "could not discover a sitemap, paste a URL" message — no mention of credentials, no edit link. src/lib/scanErrorPresentation.js:37-42. DEMONSTRATED: every staging request (robots.txt, /sitemap_index.xml, /wp-sitemap.xml, /sitemap.xml) returns 401 → rendered notice: "Staging: Could not automatically discover a sitemap for this site. Paste a sitemap URL below and run the scan again." Grep of the page for htaccess|credential: false. Edit link present: false. Dev Team's handoff frames this as "the real, working two-step flow": discovery fails generically, the user pastes a sitemap URL, THEN gets the .htaccess message. I disagree, and so does the sprint file. Requirement 10 calls the 401 "the most common real-world failure, and the one where a generic 'scan failed' wastes the most time." The LiveQA criterion is explicit: "run a scan against a site whose staging URL requires Basic Auth with no credentials saved, and confirm the 401 message and its edit link appear" — that is a scan from the project's staging URL, i.e. the discovery path, and on this build LiveQA would see the generic message and record a FAIL. The two-step flow also sends the developer down the wrong road: they'll go hunting for a sitemap URL when the problem is credentials — exactly the wasted time the requirement names. The information is already there. SitemapDiscoveryFailedError.attempts carries error:'HTTP_401' on every row (Sprint 3 built that log for precisely this). The presentation layer throws it away. FIX: in describeSitemapError, when the error is SitemapDiscoveryFailedError and its attempts include an HTTP_401/HTTP_403, present the credentials message (with editUrl on the staging side) — reasonable rule: any auth-coded attempt, or all attempts auth-coded; either is defensible, the former catches a site whose robots.txt is public but sitemap is protected. Keep the paste-a-URL prompt available underneath. Test: the 401 case through the DISCOVERY path (project staging URL, no manual URL), asserting on the message text and the edit-link target — the existing test at scan.integration.test.js:346 covers only the manual-URL path. C. [HIGH — requirement 8 not met] The incompleteness warning fires on `truncated` only. `ambiguous` and `skipped` — both named in requirement 8's first sentence — are never rendered. views/scan/_result.ejs:4-12. DEMONSTRATED (two ways): (i) Staging's post-sitemap2.xml returns 404 → recorded in staging.skipped as fetch-failed:HTTP_404. The rendered page shows "Compared live and staging: 1 on live only, 0 on staging only, 1 present on both" and lists /p2/ as "will be lost if you push" — a FALSE alarm caused by an unread staging sitemap — with no warning that a staging sitemap was skipped. Grep for incomplete|skipped|could not be read: false. Mirror the fixture (live's post-sitemap2 404s instead) and the same mechanism hides real live content from the comparison entirely — a clean "no differences" while live pages were never seen. That is the silent-under-collection failure the epic exists to prevent, reproduced one layer up, which is the exact risk requirement 8 and the Risks section both name. (ii) An unclassifiable gallery-sitemap.xml included on both sides (ambiguous, per Sprint 3 requirement 6) → "✅ No differences found — safe to push." with no mention that an unrecognized sitemap was included. Sprint 3's whole include-and-flag design exists so the UI can say "these were included but unsure — check them"; the flag is carried all the way to completeness.*.ambiguous and then not rendered. FIX: (1) skipped entries whose reason is fetch-failed:*, parse-failed:*, truncated:*, invalid-url, or max-depth-exceeded → a prominent warning (same weight as the truncation notice), listing the affected sitemap URLs and reasons per side. Do NOT warn on excluded-content-type — every normal WordPress site produces several of those and a warning that always fires is one nobody reads. (2) ambiguous entries → a secondary note: "these sitemaps didn't match a known naming convention and were included; check they belong." (3) When both fire alongside a zero diff, the "safe to push" message must not stand alone. Tests for each, asserting warning AND results render together, per the acceptance criterion's wording. === REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE === 1. Scan screen listing projects; select + trigger runs the pipeline — MET, with a ruling (see below). Auth-gated (unauthenticated GET → 302 login, tested). BASE_PATH: every href/action in views/scan/ goes through url(); grep for absolute internal paths returns nothing; verified at BASE_PATH=/content-check. 2. Stateless, no history — MET. No INSERT/UPDATE/fs write/session write anywhere in the scan path (grep-confirmed). Results live only in the response. 3. In-progress state + server-side double-submit guard — MET, verified. Two concurrent POSTs for one project: 200 and 409, the 409 body says "already running." Guard is has/add synchronously before any await, so it is atomic on the event loop; scoped per router instance. Progressive-enhancement JS disables the trigger and reveals progress copy; degrades to the browser's own loading state without JS. 4. Grouped, labelled results, page/post split, links open new tab — MET. Framing copy present: "These will be lost if you push staging live." (risk) vs "Likely the new work about to ship — informational only." (info); risk section styled result-section-risk, rendered first. Pages/Posts/Other split via groupBySourceType — 'Other' for undefined sourceType is the right call (never silently dropped). See finding A for the href. 5. Slug-derived titles marked — MET. approx. on titleSource:'slug', with a title attribute explaining why. 6. Summary line with counts — MET. 7. Explicit zero-difference message — MET as text ("✅ No differences found — safe to push."). See finding C for when it must not stand alone. 8. Incompleteness surfaced — NOT MET. Finding C. 9. Manual sitemap fallback — MET. Both manual fields,
auto-opens on any non-success, pasted URL is validated with Sprint 2's normalizeAndValidateUrl (same http(s)/SSRF-range rules — correct: a pasted sitemap URL is exactly as untrusted as a project URL), everything else on the form stays. Tested end to end. 10. Typed error presentation; staging 401 → credentials message + edit link — NOT MET on the discovery path. Finding B. The manual-URL path is correct and tested. 11. Partial result — MET, and the design is right: the successful side's raw findings, all slug-titled and marked approx., explicitly labelled "not a comparison." Comparing against an empty failed side would flag everything as at risk; Dev Team saw that and avoided it. 12. Server-rendered, no bundler, progressive enhancement — MET. 13. Tests — MET for what they cover (auth, three group states, zero-diff, truncation, manual-path 401, partial, CSRF, guard, wiring, boundary). The three findings above are each a path with no test. 14. One pinned fetch, built once, injected into both consumers — MET, verified three ways. (a) Structural: createPinnedFetch is called exactly once, in src/app.js; the only undici import and the only new Agent() are in lib/net/pinnedFetch.js; the scan router receives the pair and passes the identical references into discoverAndParseSitemap and compareAndResolveTitles. (b) The Agent's connect.lookup IS the vetting resolver (resolveSafeAddresses, built on the same isDisallowedAddress the pre-check uses) — the socket can only open to an address that passed. (c) Behavioural, with the REAL undici Agent and a real loopback server: a rebinding resolver that answers public on the first lookup and 127.0.0.1 on the connect-time lookup → SSRF_BLOCKED, two lookups made. The pre-check passed; the connect-time check caught it. Sprint 3 item F is closed. The undici dependency is justified — Dev Team's claim that Node's built-in fetch can't take a userland connection-time lookup is consistent with what I know, and the alternative (connect-by-IP + Host header) is uglier for TLS. 15. Cache-Control + bfcache on new screens — MET. GET and POST scan responses both carry no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate; rendered HTML includes the shared partials/head bfcache guard (event.persisted). Via the shared layout, no per-page copy. 16. Credential boundary at the route — MET, verified. getDecryptedBasicAuthPassword is called from exactly one place in src/+lib/: src/routes/scan.js:125. The plaintext pair goes to the staging discoverAndParseSitemap call only (live gets undefined), and to compareAndResolveTitles which Sprint 4 already side-scopes. Nothing under the route imports the store or crypto (Sprint 4's structural test re-confirmed here at scan.integration.test.js:467). This is the ruling from Sprint 3, implemented as written. === RULINGS ON DEV TEAM'S QUESTIONS === UI shape (req 1): list → per-project scan screen via a "Scan" link on Sprint 2's project list is the correct reading. "A scan screen listing saved projects; selecting one and triggering a scan" is satisfied — the list IS the listing, the link IS the selection — and a second project-listing UI would be duplication with nothing to justify it. Approved. Req 9/10 interaction: NOT approved — see finding B. The two-step flow is a consequence of not reading the attempts log, not a design. Partial-result semantics (req 11): approved, reasoning recorded above. === NON-BLOCKING === D. [LOW] No overall budget on the scan request. Two sides run in parallel (90s budget each), then title resolution (up to 100 items / 5 × 10s = 200s worst case, Sprint 4 item M). A slow staging host can hold the POST open ~5 minutes; Express has no default request timeout and the progress copy says "up to a minute." Add a route-level ceiling (pass a smaller budgetMs into both calls, or wrap the whole thing) — Sprint 6 or the first fix loop after LiveQA sees a real large site. E. [LOW] The "failed" state (both sides down) renders two generic-discovery notices; after finding B lands, make sure a 401 on BOTH sides still produces the staging credentials message (the live-side wording is separate and correct). F. [INFO] The in-memory per-process double-submit guard is single-instance only — disclosed, same class as Sprints 1/2's stores, acceptable. G. [INFO] Sprint 4's item K (sitemap-page-N → 'page' though those are paginated posts on that convention) will show up in this UI's Pages/Posts grouping. Not this sprint's defect; LiveQA may notice it on a real site. === FOR THE RE-AUDIT === Three fixes: lib/sitemap (A), src/lib/scanErrorPresentation.js (B), views/scan/_result.ejs + maybe a small presentation helper (C), plus tests. I will re-run the four probes above (hostile loc, discovery-401, skipped-404 with false alarm, ambiguous-with-zero-diff), confirm the excluded-content-type case does NOT warn, re-run the pinning check, and re-verify the tree. The rest stands unless the diff reaches it. FOR LIVEQA, when this ships: the sprint's LiveQA criteria are the most detailed in the epic and they are the right ones. The 401-on-staging check specifically must be run from the project's saved staging URL with no manual sitemap URL — that is the path finding B fixes. The real WordPress + protected staging pair named in Dependencies (www.wordzite.com / staging1.wordzite.com) needs to be ready.

PASS: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 5 — ROUND 2 (RE-AUDIT) — VERDICT: PASS Audited commit 9bf89213992939fc6bb2eaeddf9d2aaea7d21bee on main. Working tree clean; committed code. Sprint file: byte-identical to the copy read fresh at round 1 of this session (git diff 04be899..9bf8921 on the sprint file is empty). No cross-version criterion. Requirements unchanged; this round is focused on what moved. Round-1 findings on requirements 1–7, 9, 11–16 stand as recorded. Scope: lib/sitemap/crawl.js, src/lib/scanErrorPresentation.js, src/lib/scanResultPresentation.js, src/routes/scan.js (wiring only), views/scan/_result.ejs + new _completeness-warning.ejs partial, public/style.css, and tests. No new dependencies. THE THREE REQUIRED FIXES — ALL RESOLVED, EACH RE-VERIFIED BY RE-RUNNING THE ROUND-1 PROBE UNCHANGED AGAINST THE REAL ROUTE A. Hostile — CLOSED. javascript: and data: locs in a staging sitemap → zero javascript:/data: hrefs in the rendered page (round 1: one, executable). Rejected at collection in crawl.js (isHttpOrHttpsUrl on every urlset entry), recorded in skipped as 'invalid-url-scheme' so requirement 6's "nothing dropped without a record" holds. The legitimate sibling entry on the same sitemap still renders and is still counted ("1 on staging only, 1 present on both"). Fixed at the right layer — lib/sitemap — so Sprint 4's title fetcher and any future consumer are covered too. Test at crawl.test.js:375 covers javascript:, data:, vbscript: through the real parse path. B. Discovery-path staging 401 — CLOSED. Same fixture as round 1 (every staging request 401, no credentials saved, no manual URL): rendered notice is now "Staging scan failed: This staging site requires HTTP Basic Auth (.htaccess) credentials to access its sitemap. Add them on the project's edit screen. Edit project" with the edit link present (round 1: generic "paste a sitemap URL", no link). hasAuthAttempt() reads SitemapDiscoveryFailedError.attempts for HTTP_401/HTTP_403 — any one attempt suffices, which correctly catches a site whose robots.txt is public but whose sitemap is protected. Live-side wording kept separate. This is the path the sprint's LiveQA criterion exercises; LiveQA can now expect to see the message from the project's saved staging URL. Round-1 item E (401 on both sides) confirmed by Dev Team; the code path is the same branch with side switched, and I accept that. C. Incompleteness beyond `truncated` — CLOSED, both directions verified: (i) staging post-sitemap2.xml 404 → "⚠ 1 staging sitemap could not be read and was skipped — the comparison may be missing content from it: https://stg.test/post-sitemap2.xml (fetch-failed:HTTP_404)" rendered alongside the results and the summary line (round 1: nothing). (ii) ambiguous gallery-sitemap.xml on both sides, zero diff → "ℹ 1 live sitemap didn't match a known naming convention and was included anyway — worth checking: …" (and the same for staging), rendered alongside "✅ No differences found — safe to push." (round 1: the clean message stood alone). (iii) NEGATIVE, the case that had to stay quiet: product-/tag- children excluded on both sides, zero diff → clean "safe to push", no ⚠ anywhere. isConcerningSkipReason excludes 'excluded-content-type' and 'invalid-url-scheme'; flags fetch-failed:*, parse-failed:*, truncated:*, invalid-url, max-depth-exceeded. Unit-tested (scanResultPresentation.test.js:59). The warning partial is shared by the success and partial branches — one place, not two copies. summarizeCompleteness is applied to the partial branch's successful side as well, which round 1 didn't ask for explicitly and is correct. TOOLCHAIN: 385/385 (up from 362), lint exit 0, tree clean. Pinning wiring and credential boundary unchanged from round 1 (scan.js diff is wiring only — verified). NEW NON-BLOCKING ITEM THIS ROUND H. [LOW, markup] views/scan/_completeness-warning.ejs nests
    inside

    (lines 21-28, 33-40). Invalid HTML — browsers auto-close the

    before the

      , so it renders and the styling survives, but the DOM is not what the template says it is and a11y tooling will flag it. Use
      as the container. Fold into the next touch of that file. NON-BLOCKING ITEMS CARRIED FROM ROUND 1 — unchanged, still open, none required for ship D. [LOW] No route-level ceiling on a scan request (two 90s crawls in parallel, then up to ~200s of title resolution); progress copy says "up to a minute." Add an overall budget in Sprint 6 or the first fix loop after LiveQA meets a real large site. F. [INFO] In-memory per-process double-submit guard — single-instance only, disclosed, acceptable. G. [INFO] Sprint 4 item K: the sitemap-page-N convention labels paginated posts as 'page'; LiveQA may see it in the Pages/Posts grouping on a real site. Not a defect in this sprint. HANDOFF NOTE FOR LIVEQA — this is the sprint where the engine meets reality, and the sprint file's LiveQA criteria are the ones to run, in order: 1. Log in, create a project against the real WordPress site, run a scan, confirm results render and links open the right pages. Watch for the Pages/Posts grouping (item G) and the approx. badge on any slug-derived titles. 2. The staging-401 check: project whose staging URL requires Basic Auth, NO credentials saved, NO manual sitemap URL — run from the project's scan screen. Expect the .htaccess message and a working "Edit project" link (finding B). Then add credentials and re-scan. 3. A staging URL with no discoverable sitemap → manual-entry prompt (the
      opens automatically), paste a URL, re-run, everything else on the form preserved. 4. Double-click the trigger — the second submit is a 409 page saying a scan is already running; the button is disabled by JS in the meantime. 5. With a real scan displayed, log out, press Back — results must not render from cache (pageshow.persisted reload), same protocol as Sprint 1 round 3. If a real site produces a completeness warning (a 404'd child, an ambiguous sitemap), that is the feature working, not a bug — report what it said. If a scan on a large site runs long, that is item D, already known; report the duration.

CONDITIONAL: LiveQA LIVE TEST — Sprint 5 (scan workflow and audit results UI), round 1
Commit tested: 9bf8921 (working tree at HEAD ab36778 byte-identical for app code —
`git diff --name-only 9bf8921 HEAD` returns only docs/sprints/state/sprint-5.json)
Verdict: CONDITIONAL

WHY THIS IS RECORDED NOW RATHER THAN HELD: one requirement-10 defect is confirmed with
evidence (below), and the remaining LiveQA criteria are blocked on two things only the user
can supply (a reachable WordPress site pair, and the browser extension). My rule is that a
confirmed defect gets recorded immediately with the blocked work listed, not held open
waiting on checks that cannot change the verdict. Dev Team can fix the presentation issues
while the environment is sorted; the re-test will then run the full five-step plan.

=====================================================================
ENVIRONMENT — the sprint's named external dependency is NOT available
=====================================================================
The sprint file names www.wordzite.com / staging1.wordzite.com as the test pair and says to
have both ready before this gate. Neither is usable today:
  www.wordzite.com      — Cloudflare managed challenge. /robots.txt, /sitemap_index.xml and
                          /wp-sitemap.xml all return 403 with a "Just a moment..." JS
                          challenge page. Tested with curl's default UA, a Chrome UA, and
                          "content-checker/1.0": 403 every time. A server-side crawler cannot
                          pass this and I will not attempt to bypass bot protection. The
                          engine's own UA is "ContentCheckerBot/1.0 (+https://tools.wordzite.com/content-check)".
  staging1.wordzite.com — does not resolve (NXDOMAIN; `dig +short` empty). staging.wordzite.com
                          also empty. Only the apex resolves (104.26.1.99, Cloudflare).
  Claude in Chrome extension — not connected this session ("Browser extension is not
                          connected"), so no browser-driven steps could run at all.

WHAT THE USER NEEDS TO PROVIDE FOR THE RE-TEST (both, not either):
  1. A real WordPress site with a public sitemap that ContentCheckerBot can reach. Either
     a Cloudflare WAF skip/allow rule for the UA "ContentCheckerBot/1.0" (or the scanning
     IP) on www.wordzite.com — a change to your own security settings, yours to make — or a
     different site you own that is not bot-challenged.
  2. A Basic-Auth-protected staging site that actually exists, for the 401 step. No
     credentials need to be shared with me: the required check is "no credentials saved →
     401 message + edit link". QA1's optional "then add credentials and re-scan" is for you
     to run, since I never enter credentials.
  3. The browser extension connected.

=====================================================================
WHAT DID RUN (curl, authenticated session; local instance at BASE_PATH=/content-check)
=====================================================================
Boot: npm ci exit 0 with the new undici ^8.10.2 dependency; server listening at /content-check.
Regression: unauth GET / -> 302 login; login -> 302 /; landing links via url(); projects
  list now carries a per-project "Scan" link (/projects/:id/scan). /scan (no id) -> 404 when
  authenticated, 302 login when not. Server log: 0 errors across the session.
Scan screen GET /projects/:id/scan -> 200, Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate,
  bfcache handler present (grep persisted = 2, same shared layout). Form: _csrf, a <details>
  "Manual sitemap URLs (optional)" with manualLiveSitemapUrl / manualStagingSitemapUrl, button
  "Run scan", copy "Scanning… this can take up to a minute for larger sites." Second inline
  script is the progressive-enhancement in-progress state; comment says the concurrency guard
  is server-side (not verified live — see BLOCKED).

REAL SCAN #1 — project "Wordzite", live https://www.wordzite.com, staging
https://staging1.wordzite.com, no manual URLs. POST -> 200 in 0.148 s. Rendered verbatim:
  "Scan failed — neither site could be read.
   Live: This live site rejected requests with an authentication error while trying to
         discover its sitemap.
   Staging: Could not automatically discover a sitemap for this site. Paste a sitemap URL
         below and run the scan again."
  <details> rendered with the open attribute (manual prompt auto-opened — req 9 behaviour).
  Only internal link: Projects. No edit link (correct: live side, credentials are staging-only).

REAL SCAN #2 — same project, manual staging URL
https://staging1.wordzite.com/sitemap_index.xml. POST -> 200 in 0.075 s. Rendered:
  "Staging: Could not resolve this site's domain name."
  and the form re-rendered with name="manualStagingSitemapUrl" value="https://staging1.wordzite.com/sitemap_index.xml"
  (everything else preserved — req 9 re-run behaviour holds).

REQUEST-TIME SSRF (req 14) via manual URLs:
  http://127.0.0.1:3000/content-check/login and http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:3000/content-check/login
  -> both "This URL points to a private, loopback, or link-local address, which this tool
  cannot fetch." in 0.003 s; the app's own login page did not leak into the result (grep
  'Enter the team password' = 0). file:///etc/hosts and ftp:// -> "Enter a full URL starting
  with http:// or https://."; /etc/hosts content not present in the response.

=====================================================================
ISSUES FOUND
=====================================================================
1. [MEDIUM — requirement 10] DNS failure on the DISCOVERY path is presented as "no sitemap
   found — paste one", which is the wrong type and the wrong action. Evidence is the contrast
   between scan #1 and scan #2 above: the SAME unresolvable host produces
     discovery path: "Could not automatically discover a sitemap for this site. Paste a
                     sitemap URL below and run the scan again."
     manual path:    "Could not resolve this site's domain name."
   So the typed DNS message exists and is correct on one path and discarded on the other.
   A developer following the discovery-path advice pastes a sitemap URL on a host that does
   not exist and fails again — the exact wrong-road cost the sprint file uses to justify
   requirement 10, and the same presentation-throws-away-the-attempt-reason shape QA1 found
   for 401 (finding B) and fixed for that one type only. Shape of the fix is the same as B:
   in the discovery-failed presenter, if the attempts all failed with DNS resolution (or,
   more generally, all failed with the same typed network error), surface that type's
   message instead of the generic discovery text. Keep the paste prompt underneath. Add the
   discovery-path DNS case to the test the way B's fix added the discovery-path 401 case.

2. [LOW-MEDIUM — requirement 10 "actionable"] A 403 on the LIVE side is presented as
   "This live site rejected requests with an authentication error while trying to discover
   its sitemap." with no next step. The first real site this tool met (www.wordzite.com) is
   bot-challenged by Cloudflare, not password-protected, and the message diagnoses it as an
   auth problem. On the staging side the auth message has an action (edit credentials); on
   the live side there is nothing a developer can do with "authentication error". Suggest:
   for live-side 401/403, say the site may be behind a firewall or bot protection that is
   blocking ContentCheckerBot/1.0, and name that UA so it can be allow-listed. The app cannot
   distinguish a WAF 403 from an auth 403, so the honest message covers both.

3. [INFO, real-world] A Cloudflare-managed-challenge site is unscannable by design. Sprint 6
   (deployment) should carry a note that clients' Cloudflare zones may need an allow rule for
   the bot UA; otherwise the first thing the tool says to many real clients is issue 2.

=====================================================================
BLOCKED — not run, needs the environment above; will run on the re-test
=====================================================================
  Step 1  create project against a real WordPress site, scan, results render, links open the
          correct pages, Pages/Posts grouping, approx. badge on slug-derived titles, green
          section framed as the action item and red as informational, summary counts.
  Step 2  staging 401 with no credentials saved, via the project's own staging URL: expect
          the .htaccess message and a working Edit-project link.
  Step 3  manual-entry prompt on a real no-sitemap staging, pasted URL completes the scan.
          (The prompt auto-opening and form preservation WERE verified above; the completing
          scan was not.)
  Step 4  double-click guard — needs a scan that takes longer than the ~150 ms a failing
          scan takes here; the server-side 409 path is unverified live.
  Step 5  results screen with a real scan displayed, log out, Back, pageshow.persisted
          protocol — needs the browser.
  Also unverified live: zero-difference "safe to push" state, incompleteness warnings
  (truncated / skipped / ambiguous), partial one-sided result, title resolution.

RECOMMENDATION
Fix issues 1 and 2 (both presentation-layer, same shape as QA1's finding B), reship, and
have the environment ready for the re-test — the re-test is the real gate for this sprint
and it has not happened yet. Nothing that ran suggests the engine is broken; what ran shows
the error-presentation layer still discards attempt reasons for at least one common type.

PASS: LiveQA LIVE TEST — Sprint 5 (scan workflow and audit results UI), round 2 Commit tested: dffc410504a1b40795c412241739dade0bf34bc0 (from the state file's last_shipped_commit — the handoff text arrived with the SHA truncated in one copy; working tree at HEAD eb022b1 is byte-identical for app code, only docs/sprints/state/sprint-5.json differs). Round-2 fix confined to src/lib/scanErrorPresentation.js + tests. Verdict: PASS THIS IS THE ROUND WHERE THE ENGINE MET REALITY. All five LiveQA steps ran against a real WordPress site (www.wordzite.com, Yoast sitemap index: post 49, page 17, learn, category, learn-types) and a real Basic-Auth staging host (stg-wordzitesecurity-staging1.kinsta.cloud, 401 Basic realm="restricted" on every path).
